questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x = – A\text{and}x = + A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x = 0$ to $\dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2s$; then time taken by particle in going from~$x = \dfrac{A}{2}$~to $A$& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The position of a particle performing an SHM is given by:

$x = Asin ( \omegat + ϕ )$

Since at~$t = 0s$, the particle is at~$x = 0$,~therefore the initial phase~$ϕ = 0$.

At time~$t = 2s$, the particle is at~$x = \dfrac{A}{2}$.

$∴ \dfrac{A}{2} = Asin\left(2\omega\right) ⇒ \omega = \dfrac{π}{12}s^{- 1}$

Therefore, time period

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = 24s$

The total time taken from~$x = 0$~to~$x = A$~is~$\dfrac{T}{4} = 6s$.

Since the time taken from~$x = 0$~to~$x = \dfrac{A}{2}$~is~$2s$, therefore the time taken from~$x = \dfrac{A}{2}$~to~$x = A$~is~$4s$.

questions.q: Two massless springs with spring constants $2k$ and $9k$, carry $50g$~and $100g$ masses at their free ends. These two masses oscillate vertically such that their maximum velocities are equal. Then, the ratio of their respective amplitudes will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum velocity is given by& ${v}_\max = \omegaA$~$= \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}A$

Here,~$\sqrt{\dfrac{k1}{m1}}{A}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k2}{m2}}{A}_{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{2k}{50 \times {10}^{- 3}}}{A}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9k}{100 \times {10}^{- 3}}}{A}_{2}$

$⇒ 2{A}_{1} = 3{A}_{2}$

Thus, ratio of amplitude is~$\dfrac{A1}{A2} = \dfrac{3}{2} = 3: 2$.

questions.q: The function of time representing a simple& harmonic motion with a period of $\dfrac{π}{ω}$& is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega '}$

$\dfrac{π}{ω} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega '}$

$\omega ' = 2\omega \to$ Angular frequency of SHM

Option~$( 3 )$

$\sin^{2}\omegat = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(2\sin^{2}\omegat\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left($1 - \cos 2\omegat\right)$

Angular frequency of \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 2\omegat\right)$ is $2\omega$

Option~$( 4 )$

Angular frequency of SHM

$3cos $\left(\dfrac{π}{4} -$2\omegat)$ is $2\omega.$

So option $( 3 ) \text{ and } ( 4 )$ both have angular frequency $2\omega$but option $( 4 )$ is direct answer.

questions.q: A rod of mass $M$ and length $2L$ is suspended at its middle by a wire. It exhibits torsional oscillations. If two masses, each of mass~$m$, are attached at a distance $L / 2$ from its centre on both sides, it reduces the oscillation frequency by $20 %$. The value of ratio $m / M$ is close to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let $C$ be the torsional constant of the wire.

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M{\left(2L\right)}^{2}}{12}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{3C}{M . L^{2}}}$

After masses are attached,

$f^{′} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M . {\left(2L\right)}^{2}}{12} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{4} \times 2}}$

$⇒ 0.8f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\left(\dfrac{M}{3} + \dfrac{m}{2}\right)L^{2}}}$

$⇒ 0.64 \times \dfrac{3C}{M} = \dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M}{3} + \dfrac{m}{2}}$

\left(0.64\right)M + 0.64 \times \dfrac{3}{2}m = M$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{M} = 0.37$

$

questions.q: For particle $P$~revolving round the centre $O$ with radius of circular path $r$ and regular velocity $\omega$, as shown in below figure, the projection of $OP$ on the $x$-axis at time $t$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As can be seen from the diagram, the initial phase& of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}\phi & = & 30 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{π}{6}\end{cases}$

The equation of motion of the particle at its initial position at time~$t = 0$~can be written as

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\theta . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$\theta$~is the angular displacement of the particle at time~$t = t$.

Since, the position of the particle at a later instant of time always lags behind its initial position at time~$t = 0$, the equation of motion of the particle at any instant of time~is given by

~$x \left(t\right) = rcos \left(\theta + \phi\right) . . . \left($2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to obtain the required expression

$x ( t ) = rcos \left(\omegat + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Knowing initial position $x_0$ and initial momentum $p_0$ is enough to determine the position and momentum at any time $t$ for a simple harmonic motion with a given angular frequency $\omega$.
Reason (R): The amplitude and phase can be expressed in terms of $x_0$ and $\mathrm{p}_0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { If we express position } x(t)=A \sin (\omega t+\phi) \\ & \text { then } x_0=A \sin \phi \\ & v_0=A \omega \cos \phi \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \phi=\frac{\omega x_0}{v_0} \\ & A=\sqrt{x_0^2+\frac{v_0^2}{\omega^2}}\end{aligned}$
Hence both position and linear momentum of a particle can be expressed as a function of time if we know initial momentum and position

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The displacement equation of a particle is given by&

$x = Asin\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) ⇒ \sin \left(\omegat + ϕ\right) = \dfrac{x}{A}$

The velocity equation is given by,

$v = \omega Acos\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) ⇒ \cos \left(\omegat + ϕ\right) = \dfrac{v}{\omegaA}$

Since,~$\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

The above equation represents& an ellipse.

questions.q:
A light hollow cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10 g , is floating in water. It is pushed down and released to execute simple harmonic oscillations. The time period of oscillations is $y \pi \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~s}$, where the value of $y$ is
(Acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, density of water $=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Additional buoyant force
$\begin{aligned} & g \rho a^2 x=\sigma a^3 A \\ & A=\frac{\rho}{\sigma} \frac{g}{a} x \\ & T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\sigma a}{\rho g}} \end{aligned}$ Now, $\sigma=\frac{10 \times 10^{-3}}{10^{-3}}=10$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 0.1}{10^3 \times 10}} \\ & =2 \pi \times 10^{-2}\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: A particle executes SHM of amplitude$A$. The distance from the mean position when its kinetic energy becomes equal to its potential energy is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential energy is given by

$U = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}x^{2}}{2}$

The kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2} ( A^{2} - x^{2} )}{2}$.

Using the condition that $K = U$,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}\left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}x^{2}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: & A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without slipping or sliding (i) in its plane with a time period ${T}_{1}$ and (ii) back and forth in a direction perpendicular to its plane, with a period~${T}_{2}$. The ratio~$\dfrac{T1}{T2}$& will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillation of physical pendulum is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{Mgl}} . . . ( 1 )$

Where,~$I$~is the moment of inertia of ring about given axis and~$l$~is the distance of centre of mass of ring from~the axis of rotation.

Moment of inertia of ring in its plane is given by

${I}_{1} = {I}_{c} + Md^{2} = MR^{2} + MR^{2} = 2MR^{2}$

Moment of inertia of ring perpendicular to~its plane is given by

${I}_{2} = {I}_{c} + Md^{2} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2} + MR^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}MR^{2}$

Now the ratio of time period is given by~

$\dfrac{T1}{T2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I1}{I2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{T1}{T2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2MR^{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}MR^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{T1}{T2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by $x=10 \sin \left(w t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) m$. The time period of motion is $3.14 \mathrm{~s}$. The velocity of the particle at $t=0$ is ______\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}=3.14=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega} \\
& \omega=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\
& \mathrm{x}=10 \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\
& \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \omega \cos \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A mass $m$~attached to free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of $1s$. If the mass is increased by $3$ kg the period of oscillation increases by one second, the value of mass $m$ is ________ $kg$.&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of oscillation is given by& $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$,~where~$k$~is~the force constant of the spring.~

$∵$~Spring is same, therefore, spring constant will be same.

Putting the different values,

In the first case ~ ~ $T = 1 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

In~the second case~ $T^{'} = 2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m + 3}{k}}$

~Dividing the~equations, we get

~$\dfrac{T}{T '} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{m + 3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{m + 3} = \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ 4m = m + 3 ⇒ m = 1$

Thus,~$m = 1kg$

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle of mass $4$ kg in motion along the $x$-axis is given by $U = 4\left(1 - \cos 4x\right)J$. The time period of the particle for small oscillation \left(sin\theta ≃ \theta\right)\left(\dfrac{π}{K}\right)s$. The value of $K$ is _____ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, potential energy,& $U = 4\left(1 - \cos 4x\right)J$

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy,~$F = - \dfrac{d U}{d x}$.

We have,~$F = - 4 \left(+$\sin 4x\right)4 = - 16\sin \left($4x\right)$

For small \theta,~sin\theta \approx \theta.

Acceleration of particle is~$a = - \dfrac{64x}{m} = \dfrac{- 64x}{4} = -16x$

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so $a = - {ω}^{2}x ⇒ {ω}^{2} = 16 ⇒ $\omega =$4rads^{- 1}$

Now, time period of oscillation is$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = \dfrac{π}{2}.$

Thus, the value of~$K = 2.

$

questions.q: In the reported figure, two bodies $AandB$~of masses $200g$ and $800g$ are attached with the system of springs. Springs are kept in a stretched position with some extension when the system is released. The horizontal surface is assumed to be frictionless. The angular frequency will be _______ $rads^{- 1}$ when $k = 20Nm^{- {1}^{}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{keq}{μ}}$

$\mu =$ reduced mass

Springs are in series connection,~

${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{{k}_{1}{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1} + {k}_{2}}$

${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{k \times 4k}{5k} = \dfrac{4k}{5}$

${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{4 \times 20}{5}Nm^{- 1} = 16Nm^{- 1}$

$\mu = \dfrac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}} = \dfrac{0 . 2 \times 0 . 8}{0 . 2 + 0 . 8} = 0 . 16kg$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{0 . 16}} = \sqrt{100} = 10$

questions.q: Two simple harmonic waves having equal amplitudes of $8$ cm and equal frequency of $10$ Hz are moving along the same direction. The resultant amplitude is also $8$ cm. The phase difference between the individual waves is _____ degree.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If two waves have the same amplitude, frequency, and direction, but are out of phase by& $ϕ$~degrees, then the amplitude of the resultant waves is given by~${A}_{R} = 2Acos \left(\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2}\right)

Here,~${A}_{1} = {A}_{2} = {A}_{R} = 8cm$

So,~$\cos \left(\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}

Or phase difference between~the individual waves is~\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2} =$60 ° ⇒ $\Delta$ϕ = 120 °$.
